lines.japanese: 「メールこないねえ」
lines.english: “No messages yet.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 週末の夜。終演後のライブハウス前には、いまだ興奮冷めやらぬ若い女性たちの熱気と歓声がわだかまっていた。
lines.english: It was a weekend night. Outside the live music venue after the show, the air still swirled with the heat and cheers of young women whose excitement had yet to fade.

lines.japanese: 口々に感動の余韻を伝えあうひとびとの隅で、僕らは、姿を消した祭りの同行者ふたりを待っている。
lines.english: At the edge of the crowd, where everyone traded breathless impressions of the performance, we waited for the two companions who had vanished from our little outing.

lines.japanese: 「あのひとたち、ほんと勝手だねえ」
lines.english: “They really do whatever they want, don’t they?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, pretty normal, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 去年の暮れに、針生さんから電話がかかってきたんだ。
lines.english: Hariu had called me toward the end of last year.

lines.japanese: いわく、いまをときめくロックシンガー・御影クリヤのライブチケットが四枚手元にあるとのこと。
lines.english: He said he had four tickets to a concert by Kuriya Mikage, the rock singer who was all the rage lately.

lines.japanese: ＫｕＲｉＹａファンの山科さんはもちろん、最初乗り気じゃなかった渡来さんの賛同も得られたので、羽田班四人そろっての参戦となり……いまに至る。
lines.english: Yamashina was naturally eager to see KuRiYa, and even Watarai, who had not been enthusiastic at first, eventually agreed. And so all four members of Team Haneda had attended together... which brought us to the present.

lines.japanese: １００分弱のステージングは、かなり満足度の高いセットだった。
lines.english: The set, which ran just under a hundred minutes, had been thoroughly satisfying.

lines.japanese: 珍しく（例の発作ではなく）ナチュラルにテンションが高めな山科さんも見られたし、騒々しい場所を好まないはずの渡来さんも、それなりに場の空気を楽しんでいたみたいだ。
lines.english: I even saw Yamashina in a naturally excited mood for once—rather than in the grip of one of her usual episodes—and Watarai, despite her dislike of noisy places, seemed to enjoy the atmosphere in her own way.

lines.japanese: 「寒いねえ」
lines.english: “It’s cold.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, pretty normal, I guess.”

lines.japanese: バックバンドに顔馴染みがいたという針生さんは、一声かけてくると言ってバックルームへ消えた。
lines.english: Hariu recognized someone in the backing band and disappeared backstage to say hello.

lines.japanese: 山科さんは会場を出たところでファン仲間の狂夜さんに呼びとめられ、Ｒ－ウィングの女性メンバーが集まっている輪へ連れていかれた。
lines.english: As we left the venue, Yamashina was stopped by her fellow fan Kyouya and pulled into a circle of women from R-Wing.

lines.japanese: 残された渡来さんと僕は、適度に会話をしながら時間を潰していた。
lines.english: Left to ourselves, Watarai and I passed the time with a comfortable amount of conversation.

lines.japanese: けれど、ふたりとも一向に帰ってこないものだから、現状確認とこの後の動向をうかがうメールを送った。
lines.english: But when neither of them showed any sign of returning, we sent messages asking where they were and what they planned to do afterward.

lines.japanese: それが数十分ほど前のことだ。
lines.english: That had been several dozen minutes ago.

lines.japanese: どちらからも、まだ返事は来ない。
lines.english: Neither one had replied yet.

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、普通だねえ」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, pretty normal, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, pretty normal, I guess.”

lines.japanese: ときおり投げかけてくる恋人の言葉に、僕はしばらく形ばかりの頷きを返していた。
lines.english: For some time, I had answered the occasional remarks from my girlfriend with merely perfunctory nods.

lines.japanese: 思考は上の空だ。
lines.english: My mind was elsewhere.

lines.japanese: 愛しいひととふたり、空白の多い穏やかな時間を過ごすことは元来嫌いじゃない。
lines.english: I have never disliked passing a quiet stretch of time, with plenty of silence, alone with the woman I love.

lines.japanese: けれどこの場所は、いまだ針生さんにチェリーと揶揄される垢ぬけない僕から、いたずらに落ち着きを奪ってしまう。
lines.english: But this particular location was needlessly unsettling to someone as unsophisticated as me, whom Hariu still mocked as a cherry boy.

lines.japanese: 何故ならこのライブハウスは、ブティックホテルの林立する区域に隣接していたから──
lines.english: The reason was that the venue stood beside a district packed with boutique hotels—

lines.japanese: ──つまり、この辺りはいわゆるラブホ街であって、僕は不本意ながらそのことをひどく意識してしまっていたんだ。
lines.english: —in other words, we were at the edge of a love-hotel district, and despite myself, I was painfully conscious of that fact.

lines.japanese: フライデー、ＰＭ１０：００。
lines.english: Friday, 10:00 p.m.

lines.japanese: 体を密着させた男女が何組も、僕らの前を通過しつつ、性交渉を行うための空間へ吸いこまれてゆく。
lines.english: Couple after couple, bodies pressed close together, passed before us and disappeared into spaces designed for sexual intercourse.

lines.japanese: 僕は気まずいような恥ずかしいような、なんとも落ちつかない心地でいた。
lines.english: I felt awkward, embarrassed, and altogether unable to settle down.

lines.japanese: しかし渡来さんがまったく意にも介していないようなので、こちらも男として青臭い面を見せるわけにはいかなかった。
lines.english: Watarai, however, seemed entirely unconcerned. As a man, I could hardly let her see how boyishly flustered I was.

lines.japanese: 遅いな……どうしたんだろう、針生さんたち……。
lines.english: They’re late... What could have happened to Hariu and Yamashina...?

lines.japanese: いいかげん場所を変えたいのだけれど、依然ふたりからは何の音沙汰もない。
lines.english: I had wanted to move elsewhere for some time, but still neither of them had sent a word.

lines.japanese: １月の夜はすっかり冷えこんで僕らの体温を吸いとってゆくけれど、一度退場してしまった以上もうライブハウスには戻れない。
lines.english: The January night had grown bitterly cold, steadily draining the heat from our bodies. Having already left the venue, however, we could not go back inside.

lines.japanese: どうしよう。渡来さんも寒そうだ。近くにカフェかファーストフード店でもあれば、そこで待機するのが良策──
lines.english: What should we do? Watarai looked cold too. If there were a café or fast-food restaurant nearby, waiting there would be the sensible—
—Ah.

lines.japanese: ふと大胆な一案が浮かんだ。
lines.english: A startlingly bold idea suddenly occurred to me.

lines.japanese: この、目の前の、ラブホテルと呼ばれる施設で待つ──という案。
lines.english: We could wait inside the facility directly before us—the one known as a love hotel.

lines.japanese: なんて。まさか。
lines.english: As if. Impossible.

lines.japanese: 成田君だったときの僕にはこういう場所へ立ちいった経験があったけれど、いまの羽田タカシたる僕には、依然とおい魔窟だ。
lines.english: As Narita, I had been inside places like this before. But to the Takashi Haneda I was now, they remained forbidden dens far beyond my reach.

lines.japanese: そこは、オトナの男女が人知れず濃厚な営みをおこなう密室──
lines.english: They were closed rooms where adult men and women secretly engaged in the most intimate of acts—

lines.japanese: ──物心ついた頃からなんとなく擦りこまれてきた、不健全で後ろめたい場所という印象が拭いきれない。
lines.english: —I could not shake the impression, somehow instilled in me since childhood, that they were indecent places one ought to feel guilty about entering.

lines.japanese: いつか針生さんが、僕を評して精神的童貞と笑ったけれど、まさにその通りかもしれない。
lines.english: Hariu once laughed at me for being a virgin at heart. Perhaps he had been exactly right.

lines.japanese: 僕らはすでに子供を終えている。いまの僕らは、かつて漠然と思いえがいていた「オトナの男女」の側なんだ。
lines.english: We were no longer children. We now stood on the side of those “adult men and women” I had once imagined only vaguely.

lines.japanese: だから、そう、たとえばステディな女の子に「ここで時間つぶそっか？」なんて誘いをかけてみても、まったくおかしくはない境遇なんだ。
lines.english: So our circumstances made it perfectly natural for me to suggest to my steady girlfriend, for example, “Why don’t we kill time in there?”

lines.japanese: なんて。まさか。言える勇気はないのだけれど。
lines.english: As if. Impossible. I did not have the courage to say it.

lines.japanese: 「ここで時間つぶそっか？」
lines.english: “Why don’t we kill time in there?”

lines.japanese: 唐突すぎる問いに、僕は耳を疑って絶句した。
lines.english: The question came so abruptly that I doubted my ears and fell speechless.
“In... there?”

lines.japanese: 思わず渡来さんの表情を覗きこんだ。
lines.english: Without thinking, I peered into Watarai’s face.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんだって、なんだよ……」
lines.english: “Wh-what do you mean, ‘what’...?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、なんか困った顔してるから」
lines.english: “You looked like you were having trouble with something.”

lines.japanese: 「してないよ。ただほら、渡来さんが恥ずかしいんじゃないかなと思って」
lines.english: “I wasn’t. I just thought you might be embarrassed, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「恥ずかしくないよ？」
lines.english: “I’m not embarrassed.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは臆面もなくきっぱり言った。
lines.english: Watarai said it flatly, without a hint of self-consciousness.

lines.japanese: 「だって温かくてふたりで話せる場所ってだけでしょ？　べつに恥ずかしくないよ」
lines.english: “It’s just somewhere warm where we can talk alone, right? Nothing embarrassing about that.”

lines.japanese: やはり僕の早合点のようだった。彼女の提案は密やかな愛の誘いなどではなく、単にカフェ代わりの空間を求めてのことだったらしい。
lines.english: Apparently I had jumped to the wrong conclusion. Her proposal had not been a private invitation to make love, but simply a search for somewhere we could use in place of a café.

lines.japanese: 安心が少々、残念も少々。
lines.english: Part of me was relieved, and part of me disappointed.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君こそ恥ずかしがってるみたいじゃん？」
lines.english: “You’re the one who looks embarrassed, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「べつに、恥ずかしがってはいないよ。うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “I’m not embarrassed. Yeah, well, pretty normal, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「嘘だよ。あきらかに恥ずかしがってるじゃん」
lines.english: “Liar. You’re obviously embarrassed.”

lines.japanese: たしかに。恥ずかしいことを考えていた自分に、僕は恥を覚えている。
lines.english: She was right. I was ashamed of myself for having imagined something shameful.

lines.japanese: けれど僕だって男だ。大好きな女の子からホテルに入ろうなどと言われて、一瞬でも期待しないわけはない。
lines.english: But I was still a man. If the girl I loved asked me to enter a hotel with her, how could I fail to get my hopes up, even for an instant?

lines.japanese: いや、もしかして本当は、渡来さんだってその気があるんじゃないだろうか。
lines.english: Or perhaps Watarai truly was interested too.

lines.japanese: こう見えて実は僕以上に恥ずかしがり屋の彼女だから、自分からは言いだせないものの──
lines.english: She was actually even shyer than I was, appearances notwithstanding, so although she could not bring herself to say it outright—

lines.japanese: 「何を考えた」
lines.english: “What are you thinking about?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに、なにも考えてないよ？」
lines.english: “Nothing at all.”

lines.japanese: 僕は嘘をついた。
lines.english: I lied.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんの方こそ、顔赤いじゃん。なに考えてたの」
lines.english: “Your face is red too, Watarai. What were you thinking about?”

lines.japanese: 「べつになにも考えてないよ？」
lines.english: “Nothing at all.”

lines.japanese: ささやかな反撃に出てみたが、渡来さんには軽くあしらわれてしまった。
lines.english: I tried a small counterattack, but Watarai brushed it aside effortlessly.

lines.japanese: こふん、と咳払いを挟んで彼女は言う。
lines.english: After a quiet ahem, she continued.

lines.japanese: 「なーんだ、二人とも全然。も、全然。なんも邪念なんかないじゃん。だったらここで時間潰せばいいじゃん？」
lines.english: “Well, there you go. Neither of us is thinking anything improper. Not at all. Nothing whatsoever. So why don’t we kill time in there?”

lines.japanese: 僕はふたたび言葉を失った。
lines.english: Once again, I was struck speechless.

lines.japanese: そういう意味ではないと分かっていても、やっぱり誘われれば期待に胸が跳ねてしまうんだ。
lines.english: Even knowing she did not mean it that way, an invitation from her still made my heart leap with expectation.

lines.japanese: 「べつにいいよ？」
lines.english: “Fine by me.”

lines.japanese: もちろん平静を装って答えたけれど。
lines.english: Of course, I answered with an air of perfect calm.

lines.japanese: こうして僕と彼女は、初めてラブホテルへ足を踏みいれることになった。
lines.english: And so Watarai and I set foot in a love hotel for the first time.
